elaine: Heads-up: after the recent routing-policy normalization shipped, the console's per-route quota tile is showing a spike in 'unknown-route' attribution. Seeing ~18% unattributed on canary.
sam: is this the new header canonicalization change? or sampling window drift?
elaine: platform normalizes route headers now, but agents and SDKs weren't consistent. some proxies were stripping the 'X-RW-Route' prefix and our old client libs include both prefixed and unprefixed variants.
nate: iirc Go client helper preserves incoming header case and merges; TS helper was changed earlier to always use lowercase. So mixed casing + prefix variants = parser mismatch.
ishan: we should avoid changing wire representation. quick plan: 1) console ingestion tolerant read (try variants), 2) SDK canonicalize but keep aliases for 2 releases, 3) add smoke and perf checks.
sam: for (1) can console ingestion map and emit a telemetry tag with which variant matched? need signal to know residuals.
elaine: yes. ingestion will tag 'route_source_variant' and increment 'unattributed_after_normalization' if none matched. devex-bot: logged.
ishan: i've drafted small patches for Go/Py/TS to unify headers while preserving duplicates via last-write-wins; here are snippets:
```python
# py sdk: collapse duplicates, prefer explicit route header if present
canon = {}
for k, v in headers.items():
    lk = k.lower()
    canon[lk] = v
# keep alias
if 'x-rw-route' in canon and 'rw-route' not in canon:
    canon['rw-route'] = canon['x-rw-route']
headers = canon
```
```ts
// ts-sdk: prefer explicit route key, preserve alias
const canon: Record<string,string> = {}
Object.entries(headers).forEach(([k,v]) => { canon[k.toLowerCase()] = v })
if (canon['x-rw-route'] && !canon['rw-route']) canon['rw-route'] = canon['x-rw-route']
```
```go
// go-sdk: main helper
for k, v := range headers {
  headers[strings.ToLower(k)] = v
}
if v, ok := headers["x-rw-route"]; ok {
  if _, present := headers["rw-route"]; !present { headers["rw-route"] = v }
}
```
nate: watch out: these patterns will drop multi-value headers if not careful. add a unit that simulates duplicate keys and proxies that re-case headers.
sam: timeline: ingestion tolerant read deployed to canary in 15m; SDK patches to staging within 6h, staged releases across 24-48h. automation: add a canary smoketest that sends 10 idempotent requests across variants and asserts the console shows route attribution for >= 99% within 3s; failure triggers rollback.
elaine: filing a tracker DEVOPS-2712 for smoketest and ENG-9247 for SDK tracking. i'll post links when created.
devex-bot: automation ticket created: DEVOPS-2712. Please include owners and runbook steps.
ishan: pushed draft PRs: go: https://github.com/redwood/go-sdk/pull/823, py: https://github.com/redwood/py-sdk/pull/417, ts: https://github.com/redwood/ts-sdk/pull/1125
nate: i'll add integration test in eng-platform CI to run after canary deploy; if mismatch > 0.5% for 1 min, fail.
sam: also add a console migration note: consumers using custom proxies should map or passthrough both 'x-rw-route' and 'rw-route' for two weeks.
elaine: update 1767771289: canary ingestion deploy done; initial canary smoke shows unattributed down to 1.6%. continuing monitoring.
ishan: moving SDK PRs to staging now. will follow up with release notes drafts.
elaine: great. leave thread open until we hit <0.3% for 2 hours in prod. :eyes: 
elaine: FYI, add note to rollout checklist to verify header-case invariants in envoy filters; custom Envoy transforms caused a lot of the trouble last time.
